construction.implementation_origin: New implementation written in the isolated build directory; no other build or repository files accessed.

request.products: Unique id, name, description, source_ids referencing sources
request.requirements: Unique id, description, category (route category or *), nonempty terms
request.sources: Unique id, title, passages with locally unique id and nonempty text
request.config: search_limit/research_limit integers 1..100; ordered routing_rules with category/terms/priority/owner; default_route with category/priority/owner

shared_schema.output: schema_version, synthetic, status, validated input snapshot, ordered stages semantic/triage/review/normal
shared_schema.errors: One JSON object with schema_version, status=error, error.type and error.message; CLI exit 2
shared_schema.validation: One shared validation module in implementation.py validates requests, ordered stage handoffs, coverage, ownership, source references and exact character citation spans. Unknown request keys and duplicate JSON keys are rejected.
shared_schema.citation: source_id, passage_id, start inclusive, end exclusive, quote; offsets are Python Unicode character positions in the original passage

cross_stage_handoffs.data: Ranked product IDs, source IDs and product text drive contextual routing; validation prevents source provenance changes.
Ticket ID, route category, accountable owner, priority and eligible product sources determine scoped requirements and evidence.
Per-ticket requirement status and missing terms focus passage retrieval; owner, priority and unresolved terms persist in extractive findings.

behavior.semantic: In-memory TF-IDF cosine index, casefolded Unicode word tokens, score descending then ID ascending. Only positive scores returned. Optional injected embedding(text) callable adds positive cosine similarity; vectors must be finite numeric lists/tuples with consistent dimensions. No live provider.
behavior.triage: Each matching ticket term contributes 3; each matching selected-product-context term contributes 1. Highest rule score wins; configuration order breaks ties; default route handles zero matches. Priority and accountable owner are explicit configuration values.
behavior.review: Each applicable requirement selects the single eligible passage matching most whole-word phrases; ties use source and passage ID. All terms yields supported, some partial, none missing. Exact evidence and missing terms are preserved. This is a literal-evidence heuristic, not entailment or certification.
behavior.normal: Retrieves passages only from routed product sources using missing terms (otherwise requirement terms) and requirement description. Extracts the sentence with greatest query-token overlap; earliest sentence wins ties. Findings are exact quotes, never generated claims. Research does not silently resolve review gaps.
behavior.empty_data: Empty products, tickets, requirements or passages are valid if references remain valid. No search hit yields no eligible sources and no fabricated evidence.
behavior.determinism: Stable scores and tie rules; input is deep-copied and not mutated. Injected callables must themselves be deterministic for repeatable results.
behavior.synthetic_fixtures: Example includes one relevant charger, one irrelevant fan, one warranty ticket, supported/partial/missing evidence, and an unrelated source that must not close gaps.

included: One integrated CLI and library pipeline with shared schema and validation
CLI JSON validation and file-error handling
excluded: Live providers, networks, external packages, agents and git
Enterprise persistence, authentication, concurrent services and deployment
Semantic entailment, certification, legal or compliance judgments
Model training, learned classifiers and generated research conclusions

test_outcomes.coverage: All four stages, embedding fixtures and failures, source isolation, handoff tampering, route ownership, exact Unicode/newline citations, edge cases, malformed input, and CLI success/file/usage/JSON errors.
